subject: MSA/Order Form — proposed split on emergency remedies and enforceability

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Legal Ops <legal@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/Order Form — proposed split on emergency remedies and enforceability

Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is Redwood's clean redline (Acme_MSA_redline_v3.docx) that pulls together the items we discussed for the MSA + Order Form. Two quick asks from our side before we move to signatures:

1) Emergency remedies carve: we propose a narrow, mutual carveout that preserves a party's right to seek provisional/interim injunctive relief in local courts for urgent IP/data-theft situations, while the broader dispute resolution path remains arbitration.

2) Recognition/enforcement assistance: where a court issues a provisional measure, both parties agree to cooperate to seek recognition in the arbitral seat if required (mutual assistance clause).

We put the specific proposed language in the attached extract (MSA_emergency-measures-extract.pdf) — see Section 12.3 (provisional measures) and 19.1 (governing law / seat). Highlighted items:
- Governing law: Redwood requested state law of incorporation (Delaware) for US customers; we can discuss alternatives for EU/EMEA headquartered customers.
- Arbitral seat vs. forum: default to arbitration (ICC/LCIA) with the limited carveout described above.

Can you confirm whether Acme can accept the carveout as written or whether you need different language around "recognition of provisional measures" and the mechanics for seeking expedited relief? Also: any internal preference on governing law (Delaware v. New York) we should know about?

If helpful, Naomi (CC'd) can jump in with the legal compromise language; Marissa (VP Sales) is copied to confirm deal timeline if we can get alignment.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — proposed split on emergency remedies and enforceability

Karthik —

Thanks for the redline and the extract. Quick reactions from Acme legal: we appreciate the effort to narrow the carveout, but we have two primary concerns:

1) Interim measures enforceability: in several of our jurisdictions (notably in the EU and the UK) courts are reluctant to issue provisional measures that are effective across borders unless the seat/recognition path is clear. We need more explicit commitments about assistance and expedited cooperation (e.g., a 3-business-day turnaround on mutual evidence preservation requests).

2) Governing law/venue: Acme prefers New York law for SaaS agreements (even for Delaware entities) because it is more predictable for our risk team. We also prefer an arbitral seat that is neutral (London or Singapore depending on the region).

Can Redwood accept: (a) a short SLA-style cooperation timeline for recognition/assistance requests related to provisional measures and (b) New York law with London seat for international deals?

If you can send suggested wording for the SLA/cooperation steps, that will help move this along. There may be a parallel procurement approval for the carveout; I'll pull in procurement as we iterate.

—Emily
Emily Stone
Senior Counsel, AcmeCloud

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — proposed split on emergency remedies and enforceability

Emily —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Proposed middle-ground that our legal team (Naomi & Olga) recommends:

- Governing law: accept New York law for this transaction (we can make it regionally mapped but agree New York for US/Global commercial predictability).

- Arbitral seat: accept London as default seat for international deals; for strictly US-only customers we can retain an agreed US seat (New York). We'll add a clause allowing parties to agree on a different seat by written confirmation on the Order Form.

- Provisional measures cooperation: Redwood will agree to a short cooperation window: upon receiving a formal request to assist in recognition of a provisional measure, Redwood will (i) confirm receipt within 24 hours, (ii) provide available evidentiary support within 3 business days, and (iii) prioritize internal escalation to our legal ops team. We will also explicitly permit temporary injunctive relief sought in claimant's local courts for the narrow categories listed (IP theft, credential compromise, exfiltration of customer data).

Draft wording (proposal to insert into Section 12.3):
"
12.3 Interim Relief and Recognition. Notwithstanding the Parties' agreement to resolve disputes by arbitration, either Party may seek provisional or interim injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction for the narrow purposes of preventing imminent and irreparable harm to its intellectual property rights or customer data security. Following the issuance of any such provisional measure, the Parties shall promptly cooperate to seek recognition and enforcement of such measure in the arbitral seat and shall respond to reasonable requests for evidence and assistance as follows: (a) acknowledge receipt of any enforcement assistance request within 24 hours; (b) produce readily available supporting evidence within three (3) business days; and (c) escalate to senior legal operations for any complex cross-border recognition efforts.
"

If Acme can live with the 24-hour ack / 3 business-day support window and the seat/law compromise, we can produce an annotated redline for final review and get procurement into DocuSign. Marissa, can we hold pricing and signature deadline for EOW if legal confirms?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Emily —

Naomi here from Redwood Legal. We reviewed the compromise language Karthik proposed and are comfortable moving forward on that basis. A few operational notes:

- Redwood will include the proposed 24-hour acknowledgement and three (3) business day evidence window in the MSA. We will add an explicit "escalation path" item (contacts + SLAs) to the Order Form so procurement has clear operational steps.

- For any cross-border recognition where a local court requires a specific interim-application route, Redwood will reasonably cooperate and provide necessary affidavits. We reserve the right to seek confidentiality protections for sensitive counterparty information.

We are preparing an annotated redline with the agreed language; expect delivery by COB tomorrow. If Acme confirms the seat/law compromise (New York law / London seat for international), we will instruct finance/procurement to proceed to DocuSign under deal AC M-4821.

Naomi Feldman
